title: field-gemba-feedback-rollup-may-2028
content:
Purpose:
This note synthesizes a two-week run of customer-facing touchpoints (onsite, video calls, and troubleshooting sessions) w/ 12 customers across SMB and enterprise tiers. Goal: distill actionable feature asks, signal frequency, and quick-win patches we can ship in the next 6–12 weeks.

Methodology:
- Who: Customer Success + Solutions Eng + Product ops participated in gemba visits (see linked artifacts).
- How: captured verbatim quotes, reproductions of failure modes, and small telemetry pulls for recent incidents.
- Signal weight: frequency (how many customers), severity (impact on production), and momentum (customers asking repeatedly).

Executive summary (top themes):
1) Observability blind spots for inference: token-level cost attribution, cold-cache latency spikes, and per-model tail latency breakdowns (asked by 9/12 customers).
2) Predictable fallback behavior: customers want explicit, configurable model-fallback policies (A->B->C) with SLO-aware routing and visible logs for when fallbacks occur (8/12).
3) Cost-control ergonomics: easier per-route token caps, budget alerts, and preflight cost estimates for long-prompt workloads (7/12).
4) Dedicated capacity tuning: customers on Dedicated want finer autoscale knobs and deterministic burst windows (4/12 enterprise tenants).
5) Dev experience gaps: better local debugging for streaming responses and SDK error surfaces (6/12 dev teams).

Representative customer quotes:
- "We lost a production route for 45 minutes because of a cascade of cold-cache requests — nothing in the dashboard showed the prefix cache miss pattern." (Fintech, enterprise)
- "We need a way to tell the platform: if quality drops on model X, fallback to model Y only for this route, not globally." (AI SaaS)
- "Estimating cost for a 20k token batch is guesswork today; team disables features because we can’t predict budget." (Marketplace startup)

Detailed request catalog (grouped, with repeat counts and rough priority):
A. Observability & Telemetry (priority: high) — 9 signals
  1. Token-level attribution per request route (repeat 9): visible cost and token counts broken down by prompt, completion, embeddings, and cached-prefix usage.
     - Why: customers need showback for product teams and to debug cost regressions.
     - Quick win: add a per-request CSV export from Console with token counts (2-week).
     - Mid-term: dashboard charting by route + anomaly detection (6–12 weeks).
  2. Cold-cache spike detector (repeat 7): automated alert when a route’s latency jumps correlated with low cache-hit ratio.
     - Quick win: surface cache-hit ratio in route heatmap and add email alerting for defined thresholds.
  3. Tail-latency breakdown by model variant (repeat 6): 95/99th percentile per model, per-region.
     - Long-term: integrate in Optimize to recommend model variant selection for latency-sensitive routes.

B. Predictable fallback & routing controls (priority: high) — 8 signals
  1. Configurable per-route fallback chains (repeat 8): allow explicit fallbacks with rules (latency threshold, error-type triggers).
     - Quick win: expose a simplified fallback toggle in Console (canary) that routes X->Y when latency > T.
     - Risk: behavioral correctness across Dedicated/Private — needs SRE test harness.

C. Cost controls & budgeting UX (priority: medium-high) — 7 signals
  1. Per-route token budget with soft/hard limits (repeat 7).
     - Quick win: add soft quota + email warning at 80% burn.
  2. Preflight cost estimator for long prompts (repeat 5): integrate token estimator into SDK and Console with sample runs.

D. Dedicated capacity / Autoscale controls (priority: medium) — 4 signals
  1. Deterministic burst window configuration and predictable quota guarantees (repeat 4).
     - Ask: customers want a documented SLA for planned bursts and a control to reserve headroom.

E. Developer ergonomics & SDK debugging (priority: medium) — 6 signals
  1. Better streaming debug logs and replayable request captures (repeat 6).
     - Quick win: add a "download request trace" button on failed streaming responses.

F. Quality monitoring & regression alerts (priority: medium) — 5 signals
  1. Link evals/QA harnesses to production routes: when a metric falls beyond threshold, open regression alert and attach recent sample prompts.

Cross-cutting asks and nuance:
- Multi-tenant visibility: enterprise customers ask for tenant-scoped dashboards and ability to delegate view-only access to internal product owners.
- Private deployment complexity: customers on Private want the same Console signals surfaced without control-plane calls — requires local telemetry aggregation.
- Short TTLs and bursty traffic make prefix caching effectiveness variable; some customers want cache priming APIs.

Proposed short horizon roadmap (6–12 weeks):
1) Ship per-route CSV export with token breakdown + Console small table (2 weeks). Owner: CS + Product-HostAPI.
2) Console toggle for simple per-route fallback (canary) + server-side logs for fallbacks (6 weeks). Owner: Serving-runtime + SRE.
3) Soft per-route token budgets + email warnings (4 weeks). Owner: Billing + Console.
4) Downloadable streaming request trace (3 weeks). Owner: Developer-experience.

Suggested longer bets (3–6 months):
- Full route-level observability dashboard with anomaly detectors and preflight estimators integrated in Optimize.
- Deterministic reserved burst windows for Dedicated with explicit SLAs and autoscale knobs.

Open questions for product triage:
- How do we expose fallback logs without leaking potentially sensitive prompt content? (GDPR/PII risk)
- On Private installs, what is the minimal telemetry surface we require to avoid egress while still providing useful metrics?
- Should per-route budgets be enforced at request-accept time (hard reject) or billed with overage?

Immediate risks and mitigations:
- Risk: exposing raw prompts in logs -> Mitigation: default redaction + tenant opt-in for full verbatim capture.
- Risk: fallback control correctness across pooled GPU nodes -> Mitigation: E2E tests in release-engineering sandbox and staggered rollout.

Action items (next 30 days):
- CS: aggregate exact customer lists and business impact (who will pay for SLAs) — Anita (owner). Due: 2028-06-10.
- PM: create a concise PRD for per-route token export and fallback toggle — Priya (owner). Due: 2028-06-03.
- Eng: prototype fallback toggle in a staging branch and add simple logging hooks — Marco (owner). Due: 2028-06-10.

Appendix: raw snippets and small reproductions (high-signal quotes)
- "Cache hit dropped to 7% after push, latencies spiked — our ops page showed only aggregate p50s which hid the tail."
- "We want to 'pause' an experimental model in a canary without touching everyone else."

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a working rollup intended to seed a compact PRD. Please annotate gaps, add direct customer links (we should get explicit budget commitment for SLA asks), and flag compliance concerns.
